key_terms.meaning: A digital line whose direction and level are set by software through registers, not fixed by the circuit.
A group of GPIO pins (usually 8) that share one data register and one direction register.
The register that sets each pin of a port as input (0) or output (1).
A hardware counter that increments on internal clock ticks and can interrupt the CPU at a set count.
A divider that slows the clock fed to a timer, so tick rate = f_clk ÷ (prescaler + 1).
A CCP mode that copies the timer count into a register the instant an external edge arrives.
A CCP mode that changes or toggles a pin, or raises an interrupt, when the timer count equals a stored value.
A hardware signal that makes the CPU stop main code and jump to a service routine.
Interrupt Service Routine: the short function the CPU runs in response to an interrupt, ending with a return-from-interrupt.
The time from the interrupt request to the first instruction of the ISR, including finishing the current instruction and saving context.
A fixed array in memory holding the address of the ISR for each interrupt source number.
Allowing a higher-priority interrupt to pre-empt a running lower-priority ISR.
A down-counter that resets the MCU if software fails to reload (kick) it before it reaches zero.
A low-power counter driven by a 32.768 kHz crystal that keeps seconds, minutes, hours and date across power-off.
Switching a pin on and off at a fixed period so the load sees an adjustable average value.
Fraction of each PWM period that the signal stays high, usually given in percent.
The full-scale voltage V_ref that corresponds to the largest ADC code; code = round(V_in × 2ⁿ ÷ V_ref).
Driving one row at a time and reading the columns to find which of many keys is pressed.
A transistor or driver IC that lets a small MCU pin switch a coil or load needing far more current and voltage.
Direct Memory Access: a controller that copies blocks between peripheral and memory without the CPU fetching each byte.

takeaways: A GPIO pin is only a logic line; current, voltage and direction limits decide what may hang on it.
Timers count internal time, counters count outside events, and capture/compare let one timer both measure and generate waveforms.
An interrupt is a hardware call: the vector table finds the ISR, latency sets how late it starts, priority decides who wins.
Polling is simple and predictable; interrupts are efficient but need shared-variable care and a latency budget.
A watchdog only works if the kick happens in the right place, so software must be able to lose the kick when it hangs.
PWM gives cheap analog output from a digital pin: average voltage equals duty cycle times supply voltage.
ADC code equals input voltage times 2ⁿ divided by the reference; the reference sets the accuracy of the whole chain.
Multiplexed displays and matrix keypads trade pins for software timing.
Never drive a motor, relay or solenoid from a pin: use a transistor, driver IC and a flyback path.
DMA turns a CPU-per-byte job into a CPU-per-block job, which is what makes high-rate ADC and display refresh practical.
bank_note: Long answers here are marked on block diagrams and register-level sequences — pin to register to peripheral to software — plus one worked numeric example, so always draw the wiring and name the registers.

bank.q: Draw the internal structure of a GPIO port and explain how the direction register, output latch and input buffer work together. Include what happens when a pin is read while configured as output.
outline: Block diagram: pad, output driver, output latch, input buffer, direction bit
Direction register bit = 1 for output, 0 for input
Reading a port reads the pad (or the latch, depending on device)
Pull-up/pull-down and high-Z (input) state of a pin
Two example configurations: LED output, switch input with pull-up

bank.q: Distinguish a timer from a counter. Explain the prescaler and describe the four CCP modes with one use for each.
outline: Timer counts internal clock ticks; counter counts external pulses on a pin
Prescaler divides clock: tick period = prescaler ÷ f_clk
Capture: records count on an edge → measures pulse width or frequency
Compare: acts when count matches → timed output, interrupt, toggle
PWM mode built on timer plus compare registers
One practical use per mode (ultrasonic echo width, LED blink, motor speed, etc.)

bank.q: Explain the complete sequence of events when an interrupt occurs, from the request to the return. Define latency, vector table, priority and nesting.
outline: Source sets flag, controller checks mask and priority
CPU finishes current instruction, saves context (PC, status) on stack
Vector table gives ISR address; CPU jumps
ISR clears the flag, does short work, executes return-from-interrupt
Latency = request to first ISR instruction; includes context save and any blocking
Priority and nesting: higher priority pre-empts a running ISR
Common faults: missing flag clear, long ISR, non-reentrant shared data

bank.q: Explain the watchdog timer and the real-time clock. Give the register sequence for a safe watchdog kick and state why the RTC uses a separate 32.768 kHz oscillator.
outline: Watchdog: down-counter, timeout causes reset
Kick/reload sequence, windowed watchdog to catch early kicks
Placing the kick in the main loop, not the timer ISR
RTC: 32.768 kHz = 2¹⁵ Hz divides neatly to 1 Hz
RTC runs from VBAT/backup domain so time survives power-off
Use of RTC for timestamps, alarms, scheduling

bank.q: Define PWM period, frequency and duty cycle. Derive the average voltage a load sees, and explain why an RC or inductive load smooths the waveform.
outline: Period T, frequency f = 1/T, on-time T_on
Duty cycle D = T_on/T, in percent
Average voltage V_avg = D × V_supply
RMS heating differs from average — relevant for motors and heaters
RC filter cutoff f_c = 1/(2πRC) must be well below f
Advantages: high efficiency, no heat in a series resistor

bank.q: Compare polling and interrupt-driven I/O for reading a switch and for receiving serial bytes. State when each is the better choice.
outline: Polling: CPU loops reading the flag; simple, deterministic, wastes cycles
Interrupt: CPU works elsewhere, flag triggers ISR
Polling suits fast, rare or timing-critical checks inside a loop
Interrupts suit slow, unpredictable events and many sources
Costs of interrupts: latency, stack use, shared-variable bugs
volatile keyword and disabling interrupts around shared updates

bank.q: A 10-bit ADC uses V_ref = 3.3 V. Find the code for 1.20 V and the resolution in millivolts. Then write the equation and value for an 8-bit DAC with the same reference producing 1.20 V, and name two error sources.
outline: Code = round(V_in × 2ⁿ ÷ V_ref) = round(1.20 × 1024 ÷ 3.3) ≈ 372
Resolution (LSB) = V_ref ÷ 2ⁿ = 3.3 ÷ 1024 ≈ 3.22 mV
DAC: V_out = code × V_ref ÷ 2ⁿ, so code = round(1.20 × 256 ÷ 3.3) ≈ 93
Errors: quantisation, offset, gain, INL/DNL, reference drift, noise
Practical notes: sample-and-hold, settling time, source impedance

bank.q: Explain how a 4×4 matrix keypad is scanned and how a 16×2 character LCD is initialised and written. Give the scanning algorithm and the LCD control sequence.
outline: Keypad: 4 row outputs, 4 column inputs with pull-ups
Drive one row low, read all columns, repeat; detect row+column
Debounce in software; handle two-key press and ghosting
LCD pins: RS, R/W, E, D0–D7 (4-bit mode uses D4–D7)
Initialisation delay, function set, display on, entry mode, clear
Write: set RS, put nibble on data lines, pulse E high then low
Busy flag or fixed delays; contrast via V0

bank.q: Design the interface for a 12 V relay coil of 100 mA and a 12 V DC motor, driven from a 3.3 V GPIO pin. Choose components, compute the base resistor, and explain each protective part.
outline: Pin cannot source the current: use NPN/N-MOSFET or ULN2003
Base resistor R_B = (V_pin − V_BE) ÷ (I_C ÷ h_FE), with margin
Flyback diode across coil/motor, cathode to +12 V
Motor needs a driver stage (H-bridge) for direction
Common ground, decoupling capacitor, opto-isolation option
Never omit the diode: inductive kick destroys the transistor
PWM on the driver enable pin for speed control

bank.q: Describe how DMA is configured to move 256 ADC samples into a RAM buffer. Cover registers, transfer modes and how the CPU learns the block is finished.
outline: Source = ADC data register, destination = buffer, count = 256
Peripheral request line triggers one transfer per sample
Increment destination, fixed source
Modes: single, block/burst, circular for continuous sampling
Completion flag and interrupt at count zero
CPU is free during the transfer; bus arbitration with CPU
Cache/coherency caution on higher-end cores

bank.q: A timer runs from an 8 MHz clock. Compute prescaler and period register values to produce a 20 kHz PWM at 25 percent duty cycle, then recompute for 50 Hz.
outline: PWM frequency = f_clk ÷ ((prescaler+1) × (period+1))
For 20 kHz choose prescaler so period fits the register width
Compare value = duty × (period+1) − 1
Show arithmetic with units and state the achieved frequency
For 50 Hz a larger prescaler is needed; check resolution loss
Resolution = log₂(period+1) bits
Effect of low resolution on motor/light smoothness

bank.q: A controller with a watchdog resets at random in a plant with heavy motor switching. Diagnose the likely causes and evaluate fixes across hardware, software and watchdog configuration.
outline: Suspects: EMI on reset/power lines, brown-out, stack overflow, ISR overrun, watchdog kicked inside the wrong loop
Hardware: decoupling, ground plane, snubber, shielded cable, separate motor supply
Software: move kick to main loop, check task flags before kicking
Watchdog: enable windowed mode, use a long-enough timeout, separate clock source
Log the reset cause register to confirm the diagnosis
Evaluate which fix removes the root cause versus hides it

bank.q: An ADC must deliver 1 Msps continuously. Compare polling, interrupt-driven and DMA-based acquisition for CPU load, latency and memory use, and justify a final choice.
outline: Polling at 1 Msps leaves almost no CPU time; latency jitter
Interrupt per sample: overhead roughly tens of cycles per sample, may dominate
DMA: one transfer per request, one interrupt per block — lowest load
Buffering: double buffer or circular buffer to avoid overwrite
Bus contention and maximum DMA rate
Verdict: DMA for the stream, interrupt per block, polling only for status

bank.q: A system has a UART receive, a 1 ms timer tick and an emergency-stop input. Assign priorities, estimate a latency budget, and discuss nesting, missed interrupts and shared-data safety.
outline: Emergency stop highest (safety), timer tick next, UART lowest
Latency budget: current instruction + context save + blocking regions
Keep ISRs short; defer work to the main loop
Nesting allowed only for the safety source; guard shared variables
Missed/lost interrupt causes: flag cleared late, interrupts masked too long, ISR overrun
volatile, atomic access, ring buffer for UART
Measurement: toggle a pin and use a scope or a cycle counter

glossary.def: General-Purpose Input/Output: a pin whose direction and logic level are controlled by software registers.
A set of GPIO pins that share one data register and one direction register.
A register whose bits select input or output for each pin of a port.
A resistor to the supply that holds an unconnected input at logic high and defines the level of an open switch.
The state of a pin configured as input or of a disabled output, where it neither sources nor sinks current.
A peripheral that counts internal clock ticks and can generate interrupts or waveforms at chosen counts.
A timer-like peripheral that counts pulses arriving on an external pin instead of the internal clock.
A divider placed before the timer that reduces the counting clock, extending the maximum period.
Recording the timer value at the instant of an external edge, used to measure pulse width or frequency.
An action (pin toggle, interrupt) taken when the timer count equals a stored compare value.
Pulse-width modulation: a fixed-frequency square wave whose high time is varied to set the average delivered to a load.
The percentage of each period during which a PWM signal is high.
Analog-to-digital converter: it converts a voltage into a digital code proportional to V_in ÷ V_ref.
Digital-to-analog converter: it converts a digital code into a voltage or current.
The number of bits in a converter's code, giving a smallest step of V_ref ÷ 2ⁿ.
A signal from hardware that makes the processor suspend main code and run a service routine.
Interrupt Service Routine: the short routine that handles one interrupt source and then returns.
A table at a fixed address that holds the starting address of each ISR.
Nested Vectored Interrupt Controller: the ARM Cortex-M block that handles masks, priorities and nesting in hardware.
The delay between an interrupt request and the first instruction of its ISR.
A counter that resets the MCU if software does not reload it within the timeout period.
A low-power counter, usually on a 32.768 kHz crystal, that keeps calendar time even when the main supply is off.
Direct Memory Access: hardware that moves data blocks between peripherals and memory without per-byte CPU work.
An electromagnetically operated switch that lets a small control signal switch a large isolated load.
An IC such as a ULN2003 or H-bridge that supplies the current and voltage a load needs, controlled by a logic pin.
